info.title: Gobare Agent API
info.description: Programmatic access to Gobare coding-agent sessions. Conceptually aligned with OpenAI's Agents API; deliberately not wire-compatible with it. See the divergence list in the product documentation.

accessToken.description: A `gbr_pat_` access token. Scopes are recorded on the token when it is minted.

Error.description: Every refusal this API makes, in one shape.

error.description: Always present on a failure, and the only thing present.

request_id.description: Also on the x-request-id header. Quote it when reporting a problem.

OpenApiDocument.description: This document. Described so every route's declared schema resolves.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `session`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: Ours, not yours. Use `metadata` to carry your own identifier.

title.description: A label for people. Set it yourself; nothing derives one.

status.description: `idle` accepts input. `working` is running a turn. `requires_action` is waiting on you — see `required_actions`. `failed` is the last turn's outcome, not a dead session.

updated_at.description: Unix milliseconds. Moves on any change, including the workspace waking.

source.description: Which door created this session. Null on sessions predating the field.

created_by_token.description: The id of the access token that created it — never its secret.

agent.description: What is running, and how freely.

id.description: The agent template this session was created from, or null when it was configured inline. Still here after that template is deleted — it is history, not a live reference, which is what makes it usable for answering "where did this session's settings come from" long after the fact. The response has carried it since the field existed; it was simply never described here.

model.description: The model this session is bound to. Fixed at creation.

model_credential_id.description: The connection it runs on. `GET /v1/model-credentials` lists them.

approval_mode.description: How much the agent may do without asking.

tools.description: What this session can call, as you configured it, with any secrets removed. On the single-session read only — a page of sessions does not carry it.

environment.description: The workspace: its state, where the agent works, and the repository bound to it.

state.description: Where the workspace is. `unknown` until it first reports — a session is created before its sandbox exists, so this is what you see immediately after POST /v1/sessions. `running` is usable; `paused` is idle and woken by the next thing you send; `destroyed` is reclaimed and will be rebuilt on demand; `recovering` and `recovery_failed` are a rebuild in progress and one that gave up. A value outside this set is reported as null rather than passed through.

repo.description: The repository bound to this session, once one is. Null when none was asked for.

branch.description: Reported by the clone, not chosen. Null until the workspace comes up.

clone_error.description: Why the clone did not happen, when it did not.

preview.description: Addresses for whatever the agent is serving. See preview.md.

required_actions.description: Everything the session is waiting on you for. Authoritative — not a replay of events, so a caller that restarted gets the same complete answer.

RequiredAction.description: Something this session is waiting for. Copy turn_id and call_id into the result you submit.

type.description: What is being asked of you. `function_call` you answer through the API; `approval` and `question` are answered by a person in the Console.

call_id.description: Copy this back when answering. It identifies which call the result is for.

name.description: The function the agent wants to call, as you declared it.

arguments.description: What it wants to call the function with. Shaped by your own parameter schema.

created_at.description: Unix milliseconds, when the agent asked.

expires_at.description: Unix milliseconds, when this stops being waited for — set from the tool's own `timeout_seconds`. Null, the default, means it waits indefinitely. Past this the call is answered as failed and the turn continues; the turn itself does not fail.

object.description: Always `turn`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: Ours. Quote it when reporting a problem with this turn.

session_id.description: The session this turn belongs to.

status.description: `working` covers everything before it settles, including a turn parked on a tool result from you — watch the session's `requires_action` for that, not this field. `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled` are settled; a settled turn never moves again.

created_at.description: Unix milliseconds, when the input was accepted.

started_at.description: When the agent began. Null until it does — a turn is `working` from the moment it is accepted, including while it waits behind another one, so this is the only field that tells the two apart. `queued` was removed from `status`; this description still named it.

completed_at.description: When it settled. Null until it has.

artifacts.description: Whether this turn's artifacts can be fetched yet. Publication runs after the turn settles, so an empty artifact list under `pending` means not yet, and under `ready` means the turn produced nothing. `partial` means publishing finished and left something behind — read `artifacts_skipped` for what and why.

artifacts_skipped.description: Files publishing did not take, and why. Empty unless `artifacts` is `partial`. A file past the per-file ceiling, or one that did not fit in what the turn had left, is reported here rather than disappearing.

path.description: The path inside the workspace, as the agent wrote it.

reason.description: Why it was not taken. Written for a person, not branched on.

subagent_id.description: Always null today; reserved for delegation.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did. Null otherwise.

object.description: Always `item`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: Ours. Stable; use it as a paging cursor.

session_id.description: The session this item belongs to.

type.description: What kind of thing happened. Decides which of `content` and `detail` carries the substance. `error` says a run could not start or could not continue, and `detail.message` says why.

role.description: On `message` items only: who said it.

content.description: The text of a `message`. Empty on other kinds.

detail.description: Everything kind-specific: the command run, the path changed, the arguments passed. `examples` carries a real one per item type. `detail.event` is the *event* name — items and events share one vocabulary, and that field is the join between them. It is also how the two halves of `tool_call` are told apart: a call and its result are both `type: "tool_call"`, and only `detail.event` says which. There is no `tool_result` item type; code written from the enum alone renders every tool call twice.

EventStream.description: A server-sent event. The response is text/event-stream, not JSON; this describes one frame's data.

object.description: Always `event`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

type.description: The event's name. See events.md for the vocabulary.

internal_type.description: The control plane's own name for the event, for cross-referencing logs.

seq.description: Cursor for Last-Event-ID. Null on a transient event, which does not advance it.

payload.description: Everything specific to this event type. Not one shape — `examples` below carries a real payload for every type in the vocabulary, keyed by the type. Read the one you are handling rather than probing for fields: `agent.tool_call` carries `toolName` and `args`, not `name` and `arguments`, and guessing that pair wrong renders every tool call as an empty object.

SessionCreateRequest.description: Everything optional. A session with only a model is a complete session.

agent.description: What runs, and how freely. Omit every field and the organization's default connection runs it.

template_id.description: Deprecated name for an agent id.

profiles.description: Environment-variable group ids. GET /v1/environment-profiles lists them.

repo.description: `owner/name`. A URL is refused; the branch is reported by the clone, not chosen.

files.description: Files to place in the workspace before the first turn.

metadata.description: Your own labels. Returned unchanged; never interpreted.

input.description: An opening message. All or nothing — if it cannot be accepted the session is not created either.

id.description: An agent to inherit from. Per-field overrides still apply.

model.description: Must be one the chosen credential runs.

model_credential_id.description: Omit to use the organization's default.

instructions.description: Standing instructions for every turn. `null` clears an inherited one.

approval_mode.description: How much the agent may do without asking.

permission_rules.description: Path rules evaluated before a write.

tools.description: What the agent may reach outside the workspace: your own functions, MCP servers, and which built-ins. Everything inside the workspace — shell, files, git — is always there and is not configured here.

text.description: Shaping the final message: how much it says, and whether it must conform to a JSON Schema.

SessionPatchRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed.

agent.description: Change what runs, mid-session. The workspace and the transcript are kept either way.

model.description: Move this running session to another connection. Send with `model_credential_id`; the workspace and the transcript are kept.

model_credential_id.description: The connection to move to. It must offer the named model — one connection runs one model.

instructions.description: Standing instructions from the next turn on. `null` clears an inherited one.

approval_mode.description: How much the agent may do without asking, from the next turn on.

permission_rules.description: Path rules evaluated before a write. Replaces the existing rules rather than adding to them.

ToolsRequest.description: What the agent may call. Replaces the session's whole configuration — entries are not merged with what is already there.

tools.description: What the agent may reach outside the workspace: your own functions, MCP servers, and which built-ins. Everything inside the workspace — shell, files, git — is always there and is not configured here. An empty array leaves the session with no route to the network at all.

text.description: Shaping the final message: how much it says, and whether it must conform to a JSON Schema.

ToolRequest.description: One tool. `type` decides which shape applies; the fields of another are refused rather than ignored. `function` and `mcp` need a `name`; the sandbox's own networked tools are named by their `type` alone and take no other field. Naming any of the latter narrows the session to exactly the ones listed — it cannot enable one this deployment has turned off, and an empty list is a session with no way out to the network.

name.description: `function` and `mcp` only, and required for both. What the agent calls it.

description.description: `function` only. Read by the model to decide when to call it.

parameters.description: `function` only. JSON Schema for the arguments.

timeout_seconds.description: `function` only. How long a required action may stay unanswered.

url.description: `mcp` only. http or https endpoint of the server.

command.description: `mcp` only. A server started inside the workspace instead of reached over the network.

allowed_tools.description: `mcp` only. Narrow the server to these tool names.

required.description: `mcp` only. `true` fails the session loudly when the server will not connect; `false` lets the turn continue with fewer tools and an `mcp.unavailable` event. Must be a boolean — a string is refused rather than read as false.

authorization.description: `mcp` only. Sent to the server, never returned; a read-back names it under `redacted`.

headers.description: `mcp` only. Also withheld from a read-back.

verbosity.description: How much the agent says when it is done.

format.description: Asked for, not enforced — see design-decisions.

schema.description: JSON Schema the final message should conform to.

EventsRequest.description: One event per request. Batching has no meaning while the vocabulary is this small.

events.description: Exactly one event. What it does depends on its `type` — send a message, answer a tool call, approve, steer or cancel.

InputEvent.description: The six things you can send a session. One per request.

content.description: For `input.message` and `input.steer`: a string, or an array of `{type,text}` parts.

turn_id.description: For `input.tool_result`: copied from the required action.

call_id.description: For `input.tool_result`, `input.approval` and `input.question_answer`: copied from the required action.

output.description: For a successful `input.tool_result`. Serialise JSON yourself.

error.description: For a failed `input.tool_result`. Never send a thrown message — it reaches the model.

approved.description: For `input.approval`: whether the agent may proceed. Required, and not defaulted either way — denying something you meant to allow is a mistake, and the other direction is worse.

answer.description: For `input.question_answer`: what to tell the agent. It reaches the model as written.

model.description: Must be one the chosen credential runs. A session started from this agent may override it.

model_credential_id.description: Omit to use the organization's default.

instructions.description: Standing instructions every session started from this agent begins with.

tools.description: What the agent may reach outside the workspace: your own functions, MCP servers, and which built-ins. Everything inside the workspace — shell, files, git — is always there and is not configured here.

text.description: Shaping the final message: how much it says, and whether it must conform to a JSON Schema.

events.description: Empty or absent means every event.

subdomain.description: 2–63 characters of a–z, 0–9 and hyphens. Omit and one is derived from the session.

key.description: The provider key. Verified against the provider before it is stored, and returned nowhere afterwards.

provider.description: Which vendor issued the key. Only needed when the prefix does not say: several vendors issue keys starting with `sk-`, and we ask rather than send your secret to vendors you never named.

model.description: Omit to accept the connector's default.

base_url.description: For `custom`, and for self-hosted or proxied endpoints.

label.description: A name for the Console's list. Defaults to the provider's.

default.description: Whether sessions naming no credential get this one. The first connection is always the default. Must be a boolean — a string is refused rather than read as false, because this decides whose bill every future turn lands on.

files.description: Files to write into the running workspace. Same shape as `environment.files`, which seeds one before the first turn.

SeedFile.description: One file, inline. There is no Files API to reference and we do not fetch URLs on your behalf; for a large input use `environment.repo`.

type.description: Optional, and `inline` is the only value. Named rather than defaulted: a caller sending `file_id` has a file we cannot reach, and treating it as inline would hand them an empty workspace with no reason why.

path.description: Where in the workspace to write it. Confined to the workspace directory.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64. Always base64, including for text — one encoding to get right rather than two.

WorkspaceFileTree.description: The files in a session's workspace, as of the last snapshot. Not the live sandbox — `captured_at` says which moment this is, because reading a stale file and believing it current is the failure this field exists to prevent.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

captured_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the snapshot. Null means none has been taken, which is not the same as an empty workspace.

state.description: `missing` means there is no snapshot yet — call POST /files/refresh.

truncated.description: The archive is read with a byte ceiling; past it the listing stops.

object.description: Always `workspace_file`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

readable.description: False for a directory, and for paths this API withholds — environment files and key material.

object.description: Always `workspace_file.content`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

captured_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the snapshot this came from.

content.description: Text as text; anything else base64. `encoding` says which.

truncated.description: Text past the inline ceiling is cut. Only ever true for text.

ModelConnectorCatalog.description: The model providers this deployment can connect. Served without a token, like the OpenAPI document: it describes what the API supports rather than anything inside an organization.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `model_connector`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: What to send as `provider` when connecting a key.

default_model.description: What you get by omitting `model`, and what `agent.model` must match unless you name another.

key_prefix.description: How this vendor's keys begin. Several vendors share `sk-`, which is why connecting one of those asks for `provider` — this is how you tell which ids collide before sending a secret.

protocol.description: The wire protocol, which decides what a custom `base_url` must speak.

Fork.description: A new session branched from another, with its workspace and transcript. It spends a session slot like any other, and is refused by the same ceiling with the same code.

forked_from.description: The session this was branched from. It is untouched.

workspace_copied.description: Whether the workspace came with it. False means the fork starts empty — a fork is still useful without it, and believing the files are there when they are not is worse than knowing.

object.description: Always `preview`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

subdomain.description: The label the site is served under.

url.description: The public address. A Gobare origin, never the sandbox provider's.

published_url.description: The same address, under the name the session object uses for it. A session carries two — `preview.url` needs a token, `preview.published_url` does not — and this call returned only `url`, so nothing in the shape said which one you were holding. It is the public one; this field says so rather than leaving you to bet on it.

object.description: Always `preview.deleted`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `session.deleted`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `input.accepted`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

queued.description: The session was busy; the message is durably queued and will run.

name.description: Unique across both types: the agent sees one list.

url.description: mcp: the server's address. Exclusive with `command`.

command.description: mcp: a command run inside the sandbox. Exclusive with `url`.

allowed_tools.description: mcp: restrict the agent to these tools from this server. Absent means all of them.

required.description: mcp: the session fails if this server will not connect. Absent means optional, which produces an `mcp.unavailable` event instead.

redacted.description: Names of the secret values withheld from this response, such as `authorization` or `headers.x-api-key`. Not a request field: sending it back is refused, so an edited read-back cannot silently drop your credentials.

description.description: function: what the function is for. The model reads it.

parameters.description: function: a JSON Schema for the arguments. Carried unexamined.

timeout_seconds.description: function: how long to wait for your process to answer this call.

object.description: Always `session.tools`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

session_id.description: The session this configuration applies to.

tools.description: The configuration as sent, in the same vocabulary: one entry per tool, each with a `type` of `mcp` or `function`. Secret values are withheld — see `redacted`.

text.description: Output shaping, or null when none was set. Asked of the model, not enforced.

format.description: `{type: "json_schema", schema: {…}}` — the shape the model is asked to answer in.

WebhookSubscriptionCreated.description: The secret appears in this response only. Store it; it cannot be shown again.

object.description: Always `webhook.subscription`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: Ours. Use it to delete the subscription.

url.description: Where deliveries go. Must be https.

events.description: Which events to deliver. An empty list means all of them.

active.description: False once deliveries have been given up on. See webhooks.md on retries and dead letters.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

WebhookSubscription.description: An endpoint subscribed to session events. The secret is returned only when it is created.

object.description: Always `webhook.subscription`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

url.description: Where deliveries are POSTed. https only.

events.description: What this endpoint is subscribed to.

WebhookDeliveryHealth.description: Whether this endpoint is actually receiving anything. Deliveries are retried six times over roughly nine hours and then given up on; without this, an integration whose endpoint broke found out by noticing it had stopped receiving events — the one thing webhooks exist to stop anyone having to do.

pending.description: Owed and not yet delivered, including ones waiting on a retry.

dead.description: Given up on after six attempts. A number that keeps climbing means the endpoint is broken, not busy.

last_error.description: Why the most recent one was given up on, as we saw it — a status, or the transport error.

last_failed_at.description: Unix milliseconds of that delivery. Null when none has been given up on.

Artifact.description: An immutable copy of a file a turn published. Survives the sandbox being paused or reclaimed.

object.description: Always `artifact`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

id.description: Ours. Use it to fetch the bytes.

path.description: Where it was in the workspace when it was published.

content_type.description: Guessed from the path. `application/octet-stream` when unrecognised.

created_at.description: Unix milliseconds, when it was published.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

ArtifactContent.description: The bytes. Content-Type is the artifact's own.

WorkspaceFileList.description: What was written into the workspace. A path that was already there has been overwritten — that is what the request asked for.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `workspace_file`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

ArtifactArchive.description: A POSIX tar of every artifact, streamed. Narrowed to one turn with ?turn_id=, in which case entries carry the workspace path; otherwise each entry is prefixed with its turn id, because the same path published by two turns is two files. An artifact whose stored copy is gone is omitted.

EnvironmentTemplate.description: A named configuration copied into a session at creation. Changing or deleting it does not affect sessions already created from it.

object.description: Always `environment_template`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

tools.description: Tools every session started from this agent gets, unless it replaces them. Secrets are withheld — see `redacted` on an entry.

text.description: Output shaping copied into every session started from this agent.

id.description: Ours. Pass it as `agent.id` when creating a session.

name.description: Yours, for recognising it. Not an identifier.

model.description: The model sessions from this agent run on, unless they override it.

instructions.description: Standing instructions given to every session started from this agent.

tools.description: Tools every session started from this agent gets, unless it replaces them. Secrets are withheld — see `redacted` on an entry.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `model_credential`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

label.description: Yours, from the Console. For recognising the connection.

is_default.description: Whether a session that names no credential gets this one.

last4.description: The last four characters of the key. On create only; the key itself is never returned.

verified.description: Whether the provider accepted a probe before this was stored.

object.description: Always `list`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.
Always `environment_profile`. Names the shape, so a value can be identified without knowing which call returned it.

status.description: Always `ok`, and structurally unable to be anything else — it reports that this deployment answered, which is all a health check can promise about itself. It is not a verdict on your token. `usable` is.

scopes.description: What the presented token may do. Empty means it may do nothing here.

usable.description: Whether this token can do anything under /v1 at all. `false` for one holding only `cli`, which is a real token for `gobare pi import` and refused by every route here. That token reads `{"status":"ok","scopes":["cli"]}` and then 403s on the first real call — the signal was in `scopes` all along, but only for a caller who already knew what to compare it against.

missing_scopes.description: What to mint instead, named rather than inferred. Empty when `usable` is true.

get.description: Check the access token and report what it may do.

200.description: Check the access token and report what it may do.

400.description: `invalid_request`. A query parameter this endpoint does not take. Refused rather than ignored, because an ignored filter answers with everything and looks like a filter that matched.

401.description: The access token is missing, unrecognised, expired or revoked.

403.description: The token is valid but may not perform this call. The message names the scope it wanted.

404.description: No such endpoint, or the public API is not enabled on this deployment.

429.description: `rate_limit_exceeded`. The token is past its allowance for this bucket. Honour `Retry-After`; the `x-ratelimit-*` headers on every response say how close you were.

500.description: An unexpected error. Quote the request id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to return, 1–100. Default 20.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Newest first (`desc`, the default) or oldest first (`asc`).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `last_id` of the previous page. A cursor this collection cannot place — expired, deleted, or never issued — answers with an empty page rather than starting over, so a paging loop ends instead of repeating itself.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only sessions in this state. `requires_action` is the one to ask for after a restart: it is everything waiting on your code.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `api` for sessions your code created, `console` for ones a person made in the Console. A list is organization-wide, so without this a second client sharing the organization appears in yours.

parameters.name: created_by_token
parameters.description: Only the sessions one token created — `me` for the token making this call. The narrowest answer to "which of these are mine", and the one to reach for when several integrations share an organization.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: One of your own labels, as `key:value` — `?metadata=job:8842`. Finds the session for a job without keeping a map of your own.
